subject: Notice: Targeted host reboots in apac3 to enable NIC affinity fixes — Jun 12 02:00 UTC
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@astratech.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Targeted host reboots in apac3 to enable NIC affinity fixes — Jun 12 02:00 UTC

Hi Olivia —

We’re planning a short, targeted maintenance window in the apac3 region on Friday, June 12 starting at 02:00 UTC to deploy a NIC affinity fix and updated driver that addresses intermittent packet drops under heavy KV-cache replication. This work requires sequenced host restarts (staggered across host pools) so we can apply the driver without rolling back traffic-wide.

What to expect
- Window: Jun 12, 02:00–04:00 UTC (we expect individual host restarts to last ~60–120s).
- Impact: Transient increased latency for in-flight requests to affected hosts and rare 502/504 or 429 responses while connections are re-established. We do not expect sustained downtime for your service thanks to active failover and sticky-routing preservation where possible.
- Scope: apac3 inference host pools only — control plane unaffected.

Mitigations we’re putting in place
- Sequenced restarts with canary hosts first, KV-cache warmup immediately after each host rejoins.
- Traffic will be routed away from a host while it reboots; the system keeps a warm spare pool to keep error rates low.
- We’ll run a 15-minute validation window after each sub-batch before proceeding.

Action items for Astra Tech
- No action required to accept the maintenance. Recommended: make sure client-side retry/backoff is enabled for 30–90s windows.
- If you use long-lived connections, be prepared to re-open connections; we’ll return a short ATL note when hosts are ready.

Attachments and links
- Attached: redwood_apac3_maintenance_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook & rollback steps), apac3-node-map.csv (host mapping for your tenancy).
- Live status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/apac3-maint-2026-06-12
- Runbook (read-only): https://redwood.app/drive/runbooks/apac3-maintenance-v2

Escalation
- On-call operations: ops@redwood.ai (primary), +1 (415) 555-0142 (pager).

We’ll send a reminder 24 hours and 2 hours before the start. Please reply on this thread if you have blackout constraints or prefer a different two-hour window within the same UTC day.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim 
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 01:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Targeted host reboots in apac3 to enable NIC affinity fixes — Jun 12 02:00 UTC

Rachel —

We’ve validated the canary today against a synthetic KV-heavy workload; KV persistence held across the restart and cold-start latency returned within expected bounds. Runbook includes automatic warmup hooks and K/V priming — I recommend we increase the validation gate to 20 minutes for the customer’s tenant because Astra reported earlier sensitivity to <30s blips.

Also adding a note to ops: if we see >0.5% 5xx at the first validation gate for this tenancy, abort and roll back the driver on the remaining hosts.

Rafael
Director, Infrastructure Reliability

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick questions. Answers inline below.

1) Behavior for in-flight requests
- Our edge will try a single seamless proxy-level retry for idempotent tokenization/embedding calls where safe; for stateful or long-lived streaming HTTP connections, the connection will be closed and clients should re-establish. SDKs using our official client have built-in retry/backoff for short connection resets and will re-open streams automatically in most cases.

2) Billing reconciliation blackout (02:30–02:40 UTC)
- We can and will schedule your tenant’s host restart sub-batches to avoid that 10-minute window. I’ve added a tenant-level hold to the runbook; we’ll run your hosts before 02:30 and complete the final validation/last host restart after 02:40 to keep that window clean.

Attachments and links (re-attached here)
- redwood_apac3_maintenance_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook & rollback steps)
- apac3-node-map.csv (host mapping for your tenancy)

Next steps
- We’ll send a reminder 24 hours and 2 hours prior. Ops will post a live update in the status page during the window.

If anything else is urgent, loop in Rafael and Monica; Rafael is ops lead for the rollout and Monica is assigned as the customer success point-of-contact for your tenancy during the window.

Thanks —
